why: every host block is a hosts-view row: the alias you type, user@target:port as the detail, the file it came from, and the known_hosts mark
setup:
mkdir -p "$HOME/.ssh" && printf 'Host prod
  HostName 10.9.8.7
  User deploy
  Port 2222
  IdentityFile ~/.ssh/prodkey
Host dev
  HostName devbox.internal
Host *
  User root
' > "$HOME/.ssh/config" && printf '[10.9.8.7]:2222 ssh-ed25519 AAAAfixture
devbox.internal ssh-ed25519 AAAAfixture
' > "$HOME/.ssh/known_hosts"

why: a default-port host reads name-only, and 'Host *' is a defaults block, not a machine — it makes no row
setup:
mkdir -p "$HOME/.ssh" && printf 'Host prod
  HostName 10.9.8.7
  User deploy
  Port 2222
Host dev
  HostName devbox.internal
Host *
  User root
' > "$HOME/.ssh/config" && printf 'devbox.internal ssh-ed25519 AAAAfixture
' > "$HOME/.ssh/known_hosts"

why: a query matches the alias, the address or the user@host string
setup:
mkdir -p "$HOME/.ssh" && printf 'Host prod
  HostName 10.9.8.7
  User deploy
  Port 2222
Host dev
  HostName devbox.internal
' > "$HOME/.ssh/config"

why: no known_hosts means the mark drops out rather than reading 'never connected'
setup:
mkdir -p "$HOME/.ssh" && printf 'Host prod
  HostName 10.9.8.7
  User deploy
' > "$HOME/.ssh/config" && rm -f "$HOME/.ssh/known_hosts"

why: a name no host carries is silence, not an error row
